Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

This document defines optional Transition Request preconditions that let a caller state which Workflow instance observation it expected before requesting a state change.

These preconditions are domain-level conflict checks. They do not define database locks, transaction isolation, distributed concurrency, or retry policy.

Terminology

Expected Current State is a caller-supplied State identifier that must match the instance's current State before a Transition Request can proceed.

Expected Workflow Instance Revision is a caller-supplied opaque Workflow instance revision that must match the observed Workflow instance revision before a Transition Request can proceed.

Workflow State Conflict is a failed Transition Request caused by an expected current State or expected Workflow instance revision not matching the actual Workflow instance observation.

Requirements

  • WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-001 - A Transition Request that omits Expected Current State MUST NOT perform an expected-current-state precondition check. Omission MUST NOT imply the initial State, latest State, any terminal State, or any implementation default.
  • WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-002 - A Transition Request that supplies Expected Current State MUST validate it as a declared State in the instance's governing Workflow Definition Version before using it as a precondition.
  • WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-003 - A Transition Request that supplies Expected Current State MUST fail with FINKORE_WORKFLOW_STATE_CONFLICT when the supplied value does not exactly match the instance's current State before transition validation.
  • WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-004 - A Transition Request that omits Expected Workflow Instance Revision MUST NOT perform an expected-revision precondition check. Omission MUST NOT imply a latest revision, storage version, Entity Revision, or implementation default.
  • WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-005 - A Transition Request that supplies Expected Workflow Instance Revision MUST compare it exactly with the observed Workflow Instance Revision before transition validation. If the observed instance has no Workflow Instance Revision, or if the values differ, the request MUST fail with FINKORE_WORKFLOW_STATE_CONFLICT.
  • WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-006 - A Transition Request that passes expected-current-state and expected-revision preconditions MUST still satisfy all applicable terminal-state, declared-transition, target-state, and guard requirements before the current State can change.
  • WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-007 - A Transition Request rejected by an expected-current-state or expected-revision conflict MUST leave current State, Bound Workflow Definition Version, and Workflow Instance Revision unchanged.
  • WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-008 - Expected-current-state and expected-revision preconditions MUST NOT be treated as storage locks, distributed coordination, database transaction isolation, or a rule for selecting a winner between concurrent Transition Requests.
    Evidence & context6 research notes · 2 practitioner accounts+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Notes from the same study are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Idempotent request identity includes content and an explicitly bounded effect ↗

    Mikhaylov Bogdan; Omorov Akzholbek; Izripov Iusup

    These boundaries distinguish non-mutating domain rejection and duplicate-event rejection from a general command-key/retry protocol. The source’s request identity recommendation remains application policy.

    Scope and limitations

    Reviewer scenario: a lost response leads to retrying with the same key but a changed amount. Treating this as the same financial instruction can suppress a legitimate change or misidentify the result. Atomic key storage is the paper’s design; a key alone does not coordinate every external effect.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Locally valid states do not imply a global serial order ↗

    Tim Soethout; Tijs van der Storm; Jurgen J. Vinju

    Complete-result validation and supplied conflict preconditions do not establish global serializability. PSAC intentionally has weaker isolation; no universal database isolation level is inferred.

    Scope and limitations

    A global serial order is not required for every application. The source intentionally offers weaker isolation with potential throughput benefits; this is not a hidden defect. Financial implications depend on the composing policy.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Producer idempotence does not settle application-effect uniqueness ↗

    Jyothirmai Gurramula

    Duplicate Audit identity rejection and conflict preconditions have bounded domain meaning. Producer guarantees and application-effect uniqueness need their own scope; no broker protocol, cached result or end-to-end exactly-once guarantee is supplied.

    Scope and limitations

    The crash-after-effect-before-acknowledgement scenario is reviewer inference. Broker guarantees have a useful defined scope. Application deduplication still needs defined keys, retention, durable recovery and a consistent effect boundary; the abstract does not establish those details.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Preventing an invalid state does not guarantee eventual completion ↗

    Acep Taryana; Dieky Adzkiya; Muhammad Syifa’ul Mufid; Imam Mukhlash

    Valid transitions, intentional terminal states and non-mutating rejection do not establish fairness or per-request eventual completion. The hospital study supplies methodological context, not financial execution evidence or a universal deadline.

    Scope and limitations

    This is methodological transfer from healthcare, not a financial rule demonstrated by that study. Fairness, resource availability and admissible requests matter. An intentionally terminal state is not a deadlock defect; statistical confidence is not an unconditional proof for arbitrary executions.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Snapshot coherence and freshness are separate properties ↗

    Dan R. K. Ports; Austin T. Clements; Irene Zhang; Samuel Madden; Barbara Liskov

    Explicit context and supplied-observation checks do not certify a coherent or sufficiently recent remote snapshot. The cache source distinguishes coherence from age; acceptable age and isolation remain composing-application choices.

    Scope and limitations

    These financial scenarios are reviewer inferences. A consistent snapshot can be appropriate within an application’s bound. TxCache does not remove the database’s anomalies or establish universal safe staleness for financial authorization.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Convergence does not by itself promise permanence after a response ↗

    Dina Borrego; Nuno Preguiça; Elisa Gonzalez Boix; Carla Ferreira

    The source explicitly permits discarding some operations after a response. That tradeoff does not authorize erasing committed history or rewriting preserved source facts; portable reversal requires its declared evidence. Distributed confirmation and concrete accounting consequences remain separate.

    Scope and limitations

    An external action triggered by a later-discarded result is reviewer inference. A clearly provisional response may be appropriate. The source explicitly acknowledges the limitation; this review does not declare its framework generally unsuitable or its proofs invalid.

    Legacy / Clarifies a boundary

    A deployment rollback plan and a rejected-operation guarantee have different boundaries ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Workflow preconditions explicitly do not provide distributed coordination or transaction isolation.

    Scope and limitations

    The interviewee frames this as advice, not a reported deployment protocol or proof of atomic recovery. Deployment rollback, external compensation, restoration of a committed action and local non-mutation on rejection are distinct. FinKore does not supply a rollback engine, distributed transaction protocol, migration workflow, or concrete reversal accounting effects.

    Legacy / Clarifies a boundary

    Retrying a batch is not evidence that each economic effect occurs only once ↗

    Elaine Richardson

    Local expected-state/revision checks are not locks or distributed coordination for concurrent batch work.

    Scope and limitations

    This is a reported operational tendency, not proof that every retry duplicates payments. A retry after an uncertain outcome, a domain rejection and a new economic instruction are different cases. Concrete payment posting, batch scheduling, reconciliation and distributed effect coordination are outside the current Core contract. No idempotency key scheme, retention period or payment operation is prescribed.

Invariants

Conflict preconditions can prevent a Transition Request from proceeding, but they cannot authorize a transition that would otherwise be invalid under the Workflow definition, version binding, terminal-state, transition, or guard rules.

Errors

Omission in WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-001 and WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-004 means no precondition was supplied. Explicit null is supplied input, not omission. Null Expected Current State is not a declared State and uses FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_STATE under WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-002. Null Expected Workflow Instance Revision does not match a valid observed revision, including an absent revision, and uses FINKORE_WORKFLOW_STATE_CONFLICT under WORKFLOW-CONFLICT-005. A malformed revision on the observed instance itself remains FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_INSTANCE under WORKFLOW-ERROR-005. Combined failures retain the complete priority in WORKFLOW-ERROR-007; for example, version mismatch precedes an invalid expected State.

Native APIs and fixture translators must retain this distinction, whether through separate overloads, an omission sentinel, or explicit member presence. No particular optional-argument representation is prescribed.

Expected-current-state and expected-revision mismatches use FINKORE_WORKFLOW_STATE_CONFLICT as defined by Workflow Errors.

Non-Goals

This document does not define persistence revisions, revision generation, revision ordering, automatic retries, conflict resolution policy, locking, distributed coordination, or migration across Workflow Definition Versions.
